title: Lantern Walk: two worlds can share every nearby view
question: When do identical local graph views fail to preserve connectivity?
method: Exhaust all labelled simple graphs on1–6 vertices; test two elementary graph families; independently check with DSU connectivity and root-fixing permutations.
finding: Degree and triangle signatures first mix connected and disconnected graphs at six vertices. Whole multisets of exact bounded-radius balls can also agree while connectivity differs.
claim_scope: 33,867 labelled graphs, 13 cycle pairs, 8 all-windows pairs; elementary proofs for the stated families.
limitations: Not a general graph isomorphism algorithm.
No novelty, universal compression lower bound, or P-versus-NP claim.
open_questions: Which additional relation is sufficient for the next question while remaining cheap to preserve?

gardens.reason: Public learning pieces prompted the question of preserving identity when the view changes.
A playable graph toy for learning by moving the radius.
